As a **regenerative practitioner**, I work to apply regenerative development
principles — restoring environmental and social systems rather than simply
reducing harm — through community-engaged scholarship in and around Denver.
Below are several initiatives I have helped lead.

::: {.feature}
::: {.feature-img style="background-image: url('assets/img/banner-garden.jpg');"}
:::
::: {}
[DU Grand Challenges · 2018–2021]{.tag}

## Environmental Sustainability in an Urban Context {#sec-grand-challenges}

I co-led the **Environmental Sustainability in an Urban Context** cohort of the
DU Grand Challenges (2018–2021). Each Grand Challenges cohort spends its first
year in a collective-impact process to determine the group's goals; the
Sustainability Cohort set an overarching objective to deepen the DU community's
involvement with community partners, organized around four pilot projects.
:::
:::

::: {.pilot-grid}
::: {}
**<i class="bi bi-speedometer2"></i> Beyond GDP**
Developing a website that tracks, in real time, the indicators included in a
**Human and Ecological Wellbeing (HEW) Index**. The goal is to engage community
partners directly — each partner can submit indicators of interest and take part
in deciding how they should be included — building relationships through which
DU faculty and students can engage with the community.
:::

[CityCraft · West Denver]{.tag}

## Community Integrated Research Center (CIRC) {#sec-circ}

The **Community Integrated Research Center (CIRC)** was created as part of the
[CityCraft](https://www.citycraftventures.com) initiative to bring scholars from
across Colorado's Front Range together to help the City and County of Denver
redevelop West Denver in a regenerative way. The group includes members of the
CityCraft team along with CU Denver's Urban Planning Department, DU's Real Estate
and Construction Management Department, Colorado State University's Institute for
the Built Environment, and Regis University's Business School.
:::
:::
